A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are available and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic regression experiments and evaluations on UTKFace, ColoredMNIST, and SST-2 in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original synthetic, image-regression, image-classification, and sentiment-classification results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The learning objectives, pseudo-label generation, linear probing, and full-finetuning procedures are retained. The new regularization discussion concerns existing procedures; the sampling revision concerns empirical dimension estimation.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic Gaussian regression, UTKFace age estimation, ColoredMNIST binary classification, and SST-2 sentiment classification. The label-noise scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the Weak, S-Baseline, and S-Ceiling references and the same ResNet, ResNet-D, and BERT teacher sets. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 broadens the reported column-sampling procedure for correlation-dimension estimation from uniform sampling to uniform or adaptive sketching-based interpolative decomposition. This is a reported protocol revision; neither rerunning experiments nor which option produced the retained estimates is established. Other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sample-size and feature-overlap sensitivity studies and injected-label-noise experiments are retained throughout Section 4 and Appendix E. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations over 40 runs for synthetic experiments and 10 runs for UTKFace. Error-bar reporting is retained, with no added run counts, seed information, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–3 retain their result entries, plotted curves, and numerical values, including the appendix classification results. The reported performance, scaling, and label-noise findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 replaces a direct equality in the bias-bound derivation with conditional-expectation steps and an inequality leading to rho_w(n)/n. This revises the mathematical argument locally; theorem statements, assumptions, and the ridge-regression analysis remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions: an intrinsic-dimension framework, variance reduction through teacher–student discrepancy, and sample-complexity and relative-performance analysis.

C2.justification: New Remark 2 explicitly explains regularization as preventing overfitting to the weak teacher and connects the idealized ridgeless setting to the existing ridge extension. The substantive limitations and future directions in Section 5 are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a reference and computational guidance for adaptive column selection, contrasting uniform sampling for efficiency with interpolative decomposition when affordable. Other implementation settings and resource disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Goel et al. (2025) as empirical corroboration and Medvedev, Xue, and Yao et al. (2025) as concurrent theoretical work. Additional technical citations appear in Appendices A and E.3. The paper's central variance-reduction positioning is retained; publication updates to existing references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized related-work rewrites, grammar and terminology edits, expands an existing paragraph into Remark 2, and adds a funding acknowledgement. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays undergo local repositioning: Figure 6 moves off the page shared with Figure 5, and Figure 4 appears below preceding discussion. Text and equations also reflow. Figure designs, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves explanation and research context through Remark 2 and the discussion of relevant concurrent work. The empirical evidence and main theoretical statements are unchanged. Appendix E.3 adds useful computational guidance but leaves the sampling option behind the retained estimates unspecified, limiting the reproducibility benefit. These are limited overall gains, rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
